text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
Born on this day in 700 B.C was ISAIAH the Prophet.
CICERO (MARCUS TULLIUS) the Roman orator was born in 106 B.C.
Humorist and playwright DOUGLAS JEROLD, who wrote "15 Years Of A Drunkard's Life", was born in 1803.
EDWARD LARKIN was born in 1880. He was the first full-time Secretary of the NSW Rugby League, and was responsible for making the code the major winter sport in that state. He died at Gallipoli.
Australian journalist, cartoonist and cricketer ARTHUR MAILEY was born in 1886. Once dismissing his hero, VICTOR TRUMPER, MAILEY a spin-bowler claimed he "felt like a boy who had killed a dove".
South African born novelist and author of "The Lord Of The Rings" J. R. R. TOLKIEN was born in 1892.
Danish pianist and entertainer VICTOR BORGE was born in 1909.

One of the ANDREWS Sisters MAXINE was born in 1918. She died of a heart attack in 1982. After war time hits with her sisters, PATTI and LAVERNE, MAXINE recorded her first solo album in 1985. The sisters began performing together in the thirties and sold more 60 million records, making them one of the most successful all-female groups ever. HIts included "Shoo Shoo Baby" (1943), "Rum and Coca Cola" (1945), 'Christmas Island" (1946) and "I Wanna Be Loved" (1950). They sang with various artists such as DANNY KAYE, BURL IVES, CARMEN MIRANDA and BING CROSBY. They made several records with BING including "Pistol Packin' Mama" (1943) and "Don't Fence Me In" (1944).
Australian actor CHARLES TINGWELL was born in 1923.
American actress VICTORIA PRINCIPAL, famous for her role as BOBBY EWING's wife in the TV soap "Dallas", was born in 1945.

One of the founding members of 'Crosby, Stills and Nash' STEPHEN STILLS was born in 1945. NEIL YOUNG joined the group at the Woodstock Festival and 'Crosby, Stills, Nash and Young' was born. Each member also produced solo records as well as their group efforts. After a 14 year gap they reformed in 1988 to produce the LP "American Dream".

British bass player, keyboard player and songwriter JOHN PAUL JONES (JOHN BALDWIN) was born in 1946. He was an original member, along with JIMMY PAGE, of 'Led Zeppelin' in 1968. Their first hit was their biggest in 1969 with "Whole Lotta Love". The band broke up after the death of drummer JOHN BONHAM in 1980.
Australian baritone DENNIS WALTER was born in 1955.
** EVENTS **
1777 : GEORGE WASHINGTON defeated the British at the
"Battle of Princeton".
1795 : JOSIAH WEDGWOOD, creator of the famous blue and
white china, died.
1918 : New Zealand born scientist ERNEST RUTHERFORD
announced he had split the atom.
1924 : Howard Carter, British egyptologist, found the
sarcophagus of Tutankhamun in the Valley of the Kings near Luxor.
1946 : Nazi propagandist WILLIAM JOYCE, known to British
wartime radio listeners as "LORD HAW-HAW", was hanged for treason.
1958 : Sir EDMUND HILLARY reached the South Pole.
1959 : Alaska became the 49th and largest American State.
1961 : The one-millionth MORRIS MINOR car was made in
Britain.
1962 : Cuban Leader Fidel CASTRO was excommunicated by
Pope John XXIII.
1967 : JACK RUBY, who killed LEE HARVEY OSWALD, died in
Hospital.
1979 : Death of CONRAD HILTON, who founded the Hilton
Hotel Group and was once married to ZSA ZSA GABOR.
1980 : British naturalist JOY ADAMSON, author of "BORN
FREE", was murdered in a Kenyan game park. She was first believed to have been attacked by a lion.
1983 : South African Prime Minister Pik BOTHA announced

that on the following Wednesday there'd be a "national day of prayer" to end the country's long-running drought. As he spoke, a thunderstorm drenched Delmas in Transvaal Province, drowning 100,000 chickens.
1985 : The Australian dollar hit a low of 80.35 US cents.
